paper.title: Inference with the Upper Confidence Bound Algorithm

settings.name_in_paper: K-armed bandit with sub-Gaussian rewards, fixed K (UCB stability)
unmapped: Objective is stability of arm-pull counts and asymptotic normality of arm sample means (statistical inference) under UCB, not regret
Gaps Delta_a may depend on T; the optimal arm need not be unique
Arm-specific sub-Gaussian parameters lambda_a, uniformly bounded by a constant B
settings.definition_quote: At each time step $t$, the player selects an arm $\selectedarm \in [\K]$ and receives a random reward $\reward \in \real$ from the distribution $\armdist_{A_t}$. ... $\mathcal{P}_a$ is $\subG_a$-sub-Gaussian for all arms a, and $|\subG_a| \leq B$ ... Throughout we assume that $\T$ is known to the algorithm.

unmapped: Objective is stability of arm-pull counts under UCB, not regret

Arm-specific sub-Gaussian parameters bounded by a constant B
settings.definition_quote: we study the stability properties of arms when the number of arms grows with the number of arm pulls $\T$ ... $\frac{\log K}{\log \T} \rightarrow 0$

source.label: thm:bandit-stability
source.quote: Suppose we pull bandit arms using Algorithm~\ref{algo:UCB}. Let Assumptions~\eqref{eqn:arm-mean-diff-UB}-\eqref{eqn:sub-Gaussian} be in force and the number of arms $K$ fixed. Then, for each arm $a \in [K]$, the number of arm pulls $n_{a, \T}$ satisfies \frac{n_{a, T}}{\left( 1/\sqrt{\nopt} + \sqrt{\Delta_a^2 / 2 \log \T} \right)^{-2}} \rightarrow 1 in probability. where $\nopt$ is the unique solution to ...

results.notes: This is a stability result: pull counts are asymptotically equivalent to a deterministic quantity. It is two-sided and not a regret bound, and is labelled 'upper' only because the schema requires a side. The paper's main inferential consequences (Theorem 3.2: asymptotically exact CI coverage; Corollary 1: variance-estimator consistency) are not recorded as performance guarantees.

bound.regime: asymptotic equivalence as T -> infinity, for every arm a

symbols.n_star: unique solution of sum_a 1/(sqrt(T/n_star) + sqrt(T*Delta_a^2/(2 log T)))^2 = 1
symbols.B_near: constant B defining the B-near-optimal arm set S_B = {a : sqrt(n_star Delta_a^2/(2 log T)) <= B}

conditions: log K / log T -> 0 as T -> infinity (K may grow with T)
Delta_a/sqrt(2 log T) = o(1) for all arms a

there exists B > 0 such that |S_B|/K >= alpha > 0 for all T >= T_0 (many near-optimal arms)

source.label: thm:growing-thm
source.quote: Let Assumptions~\eqref{eqn:K-growth},~\eqref{eqn:arm-mean-diff-UB} and~\eqref{eqn:sub-Gaussian} are in force and the condition~\eqref{eqn:large-opt-arms} holds for some $\B > 0$. Then for all arms $a$: \frac{n_{a, \T}}{\left( 1/\sqrt{n^\star} + \Delta_a/\sqrt{2 \log \T} \right)^{-2}} \rightarrow 1 in probability. where $n^\star$ is the unique solution of~\eqref{eqn:n-star-eqn}.

results.notes: Stability statement, not a regret bound; it is two-sided and labelled 'upper' only because the schema requires a side. In the paper, alpha denotes the near-optimal arm fraction; it is renamed alpha_frac here.
